Scientific review and evidence repair

Source: vignettes/scientific-review.Rmd
scientific-review.Rmd

Citation verification asks one question: does this source say what the claim says? Scientific review asks a harder one: does the claim hide an unstated assumption, overstate scope, rely on flawed methods, or conflict with other evidence?

Tempest keeps those two checks separate. When enabled, scientific review inspects a bounded set of claims before publishing a STORM report or Co-STORM session, pairs each initial review with an independent adjudicator, and can optionally run one targeted follow-up search to repair missing evidence.

Enable review and evidence repair

Turn review on through tempest_config() (or under Workspace settings → Scientific review in tempest_app()):

library(tempest)

cfg <- tempest_config(
  research_review = TRUE,
  repair_evidence = TRUE,
  max_review_claims = 5,
  review_concurrency = 2
)

result <- tempest_run(
  "What evidence supports the reproducibility of this measurement method?",
  config = cfg
)

cat(tempest_report(result))
reviews <- tempest_claim_reviews(result)

The same configuration applies to Co-STORM sessions—review runs when you call session$publish(), once the conversation has gathered its claims:

session <- tempest_session("Measurement reproducibility", config = cfg)
session$step("Compare the core assumptions and validation evidence.")
session$publish()

tempest_claim_reviews(session)

Budgets and boundaries

Review is off by default and strictly bounded so costs stay predictable:

  • max_review_claims (1–20): contradicted and weakly supported claims are prioritized first after citation verification.
  • review_concurrency (1–4): independent claim reviews can run in parallel; each selected claim gets an initial review and a separate adjudication pass.
  • repair_evidence = TRUE: permits at most one targeted search and two fetched sources per selected claim.
  • Dossier bounds: up to 12 sources and 20,000 characters per source. Review findings remain advisory—they never alter citation verification or auto-accept claims into Graft.

Read the review outcomes

The published report’s Scientific review section reports one of four outcomes for each reviewed claim:

  • Concern confirmed by adjudicator: the adjudicator found concrete evidence supporting the reviewer’s concern. Treat this as a priority signal for human review.
  • Concern dismissed by adjudicator: broader context did not support the proposed flaw.
  • Unresolved: available evidence could not settle the question within the configured budget.
  • No issue found: no defect was identified within the dossier and budget. Absence of detected flaws is not proof of correctness.

tempest_claim_reviews() returns plain structured records containing each claim, captured source excerpts and hashes, reviewer and adjudicator outputs, search outcomes, and model/program identifiers. Those records survive session save/resume and travel alongside research artifacts in Graft as advisory context—separate from accepted claims.

Evaluate changes offline before adopting them

The repository includes tools/research-eval.R and a synthetic test corpus under inst/extdata/research-eval/ covering support, scope inflation, omitted caveats, contradictions, abstention, and misleading sources.

Use topic-disjoint training, validation, and test splits when experimenting with prompt changes or dsprrr optimization, and measure false-support errors separately from coverage.

Design inspiration

The review and repair design draws on Google’s Deep Review (bounded dossiers, adaptive attention, and independent adjudication) and the retrieval-feedback loop in OpenScholar.
